docs.text: RepoWhisper RepoWhisper analyzes a software repository and generates navigable technical documentation with a multi-agent workflow. Python scope: RepoWhisper is currently a Python code-analysis library. Python source files and Python import graphs are supported. It does not yet provide equivalent analysis for JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Go, Rust, or other languages. What it does RepoWhisper accepts a public GitHub repository URL, inspects its Python structure and dependencies, reads supported Python source files, and produces: an architectural summary; a file-by-file explanation; targeted line-level notes; a JSON document consumed by the bundled web interface. Architectural explanations and narration are produced by the configured LangChain model. Module-draft review is handled separately by the local, calibrated Laya/Vega Reviewer. The public entry point is the RepoWhisper facade. Documentation map Installation - install the project and documentation tools. Quick Start - run a complete analysis. Configuration - configure the LLM provider and analysis level. System Overview - understand the end-to-end pipeline. Output Format - consume the generated JSON. API Reference - inspect the Python API. Current scope The dependency tracer currently analyzes Python imports. Its tracer structure allows additional languages to be added without changing the public facade.

docs.text: Agents and Workflow The workflow is implemented by AgentsWorkflow using LangGraph. Architect The Architect runs after the per-file analysis. It receives a budgeted directory tree, a facts sheet computed by static analysis, and short per-module notes, and produces an executive architectural summary. It must mention only names that appear in that evidence, written in backticks so they can be verified. Navigator The Navigator receives one source file at a time. Its structured output contains: a prose explanation; a one-line summary ( one_liner , optional: the first sentence of the explanation is used when a model omits it); selected line-level notes; one-based line numbers in its model response. The workflow converts those line numbers to zero-based indexes for the final JSON consumed by the frontend. Laya Reviewer The Reviewer is a locally calibrated Laya/Vega classifier, not an LLM agent. It predicts whether a Navigator draft is an EXPLANATION or a debugging-oriented DEBUG . A DEBUG result returns corrective feedback and sends the draft back to the Navigator. This review step runs locally and consumes no LLM tokens. Storyteller The Storyteller combines the facts sheet, the module notes and the Architect draft into the final narrative and JSON payload. When facts and draft disagree, the facts win. Package summarizer A small helper agent used only when the module notes do not fit context_budget . It compresses the notes of one directory into at most three factual sentences and never sees raw source code. Grounding verifier Not an agent: a deterministic check (no tokens). It extracts every code reference from the generated text and verifies it against the names found in the repository (files, classes, functions, arguments, libraries, flags, environment variables). It catches invented names, not incorrect descriptions of behaviour. Retry behavior The Navigator and Laya Reviewer form a feedback loop: Navigator -> Reviewer -> approved -> next file | +---- rejected -> Navigator The workflow continues until all files in the dependency order have been processed, then builds the facts and invokes the Architect and the Storyteller.

docs.text: API Reference Public facade RepoWhisper The main Facade for the Excode library. This class orchestrates the entire process from fetching the repository to answering complex questions using AI agents. It follows the Dependency Inversion Principle by accepting any language model that adheres to the BaseChatModel interface. __init__ ( source_target , llm , user_level = UserLevel . JUNIOR , context_budget = TokenUtilities . DEFAULT_CONTEXT_BUDGET ) Initializes the Excode engine. Parameters: source_target ( str ) – A public GitHub HTTP(S) repository URL. llm ( BaseChatModel ) – The initialized LangChain chat model. user_level ( UserLevel , default: JUNIOR ) – Default JUNIOR. The user level used to tell the llm how the explanation should be JUNIOR: large explanation MID: mid level explanation SENIOR: very short explanation context_budget ( int , default: DEFAULT_CONTEXT_BUDGET ) – Maximum estimated tokens of evidence (static facts, module notes, directory tree) handed to the Architect and the Storyteller. Lower it for small context windows or strict rate limits; the pipeline compresses the notes to fit. generate_documentation () The main public method. Orchestrates source retrieval and automated LangGraph analysis. Returns: str | None – A formatted JSON string ready for a frontend UI if there is no error, else it returns None analyze ( json_path = None , port = 8543 ) Execute full analysis if json_path is None, save data and launch react interface locally. If json_path is passed the analysis is not executed and the interface starts immediately Parameters: json_path ( str | Path | None , default: None ) – JSON file path of a previous analysis. port ( int , default: 8543 ) – port value for the web interface. RepositoryCloneError Bases: SourceError , RuntimeError Raised when a GitHub repository cannot be cloned. ProviderError Bases: RepoWhisperError , RuntimeError Raised when the configured LLM provider rejects or cannot complete a request. ReportFileError Bases: ReportError , FileNotFoundError Raised when a report file cannot be found or read. UserLevel.MID : medium-depth explanations. UserLevel.SENIOR : concise explanations. Custom Exceptions Below are listed all the custom exceptions that the user can encounter during the use of the library. Exceptions RepoWhisperError Bases: Exception Base exception for errors that can be presented to a RepoWhisper user. SourceError Bases: RepoWhisperError Base exception for repository source errors. InvalidSourceError Bases: SourceError , ValueError Raised when the repository target is not a supported GitHub URL. Source management SourceManager Handles the retrieval and preparation of the source code. Responsible for cloning remote repositories. get_path () Clones the repository and return the absolute path to the temp folder. Returns: str – The absolute path to the ready-to-use source code. Raises: ValueError – If URL is not a valid github URL. RuntimeError – If the git cloning process fails. cleanup () Removes temporary directories to free up disk space. Should be called in a finally block. JSON validation AnalysisJsonValidator Deterministic validator for the JSON output generated or loaded in RepoWhisper. validate_string ( raw_json ) staticmethod Validate a raw JSON string. Raise ValueError it the structure don't correspond to the schema. Parameters: raw_json ( str ) – string of the json to be validated validate_file ( file_path ) staticmethod Read and validate a JSON file before being passed to React interface. Parameters: file_path ( str | Path ) – Path of the JSON file to validate. Agents BaseAgent Bases: ABC Abstract base class for all AI agents within the Excode ecosystem. Enforces a strict contract for agent implementation following the Open/Closed Principle (OCP). analyze ( query , context ) abstractmethod Executes the agent's core logic based on the user query and provided context. Parameters: query ( str ) – The specific question or task requested by the user. context ( Any ) – The contextual data required for the analysis (e.g., retrieved code snippets, file tree). Returns: str ( Any ) – The synthesized response generated by the LLM. Architect Bases: BaseAgent Specialized agent that takes grounded evidence about the project (directory tree, statically extracted facts and short per-module notes) and outputs a clean, architectural overview tailored to the user's level. __init__ ( llm , user_level ) Initializes the Architect agent. Parameters: llm ( BaseChatModel ) – The language model to be used. user_level ( str ) – Target developer seniority ('junior', 'mid', 'senior'). CodeNavigator Bases: BaseAgent Specialized agent responsible for interpreting and explaining specific code fragments read from the repository. __init__ ( llm , user_level ) Initializes the CodeNavigator agent. Parameters: llm ( BaseChatModel ) – The language model to be used. user_level ( str ) – User level decided by the user ('junior', 'mid', 'senior'). analyze ( query , context ) Processes the query against the code context using the injected LLM. LayaReviewer Deterministic System-1 Reviewer powered by a locally calibrated Laya/Vega classifier. Handles one-time caching of both the Vega reader and its underlying backbone with a unified progress bar, instant Ctrl+C exit, offline fast-boot, and zero-token inference. evaluate ( draft ) Returns the raw predicted class label for a module explanation draft. review ( draft ) Reviews a CodeNavigator draft. Returns None if the draft is a valid explanation, or corrective feedback if it drifted into debugging. Storyteller Bases: BaseAgent __init__ ( llm , user_level ) Initializes the StorytellerAgent. Parameters: llm ( BaseChatModel ) – The language model to be used. user_level ( str ) – User level decided by the user Orchestration ProjectState Bases: TypedDict The global shared state for the RepoWhisper LangGraph orchestration. Acts as the central communication blackboard for all agents, ensuring type safety and predictable data flow. AgentsWorkflow Constructs and executes the LangGraph state machine for analyzing repositories. Pipeline: Tracer -> (Navigator <-> local Laya/Vega Reviewer) per file -> static Facts and budgeted evidence -> Architect -> Storyteller. The Architect and the Storyteller run AFTER the per-file analysis so they work on grounded evidence instead of on the bare directory tree. Analysis DependencyTracer Build a dependencies graph module. Language agnostic get_ordered_processing_list ( graph ) Advanced DFS with states WHITE (0), GRAY (1), BLACK (2) to safely detect circular dependencies. ProjectTreeGenerator Generates a textual representation of the project's directory structure. Ignores common build, virtual environment, and hidden directories to save LLM context window tokens. generate ( dir_path , prefix = '' , ignore_dirs = None , max_depth = None , _depth = 1 ) staticmethod Recursively builds a tree-like string of the directory. Parameters: dir_path ( str ) – The root directory to scan. prefix ( str , default: '' ) – Used internally for formatting the tree branches. ignore_dirs ( set [ str ] | None , default: None ) – Directories to skip. max_depth ( int | None , default: None ) – If set, directories nested deeper than this are not expanded and are shown with an item count instead. _depth ( int , default: 1 ) – Used internally to track the current depth. Returns: str ( str ) – The visual tree representation of the folder structure. generate_within_budget ( dir_path , max_tokens ) staticmethod Builds the deepest tree that fits in max_tokens . The full tree is returned when it fits. Otherwise the tree is generated with a decreasing maximum depth, so every top-level area stays visible and only the deepest levels are collapsed into item counts. Parameters: dir_path ( str ) – The root directory to scan. max_tokens ( int ) – Token budget for the tree. Returns: str ( str ) – A tree whose estimated size is within the budget (depth 1 is the floor). FileFacts dataclass Facts extracted from one source file with a single AST pass. RepoFacts dataclass Everything RepoWhisper can state about a repository without calling an LLM. sheet is a short human/LLM readable rendering; the known_* sets are the full, untruncated vocabulary of the repository used to verify generated text. FactsExtractor Extracts verifiable facts from a Python repository using only static analysis. The output grounds the LLM agents (what really exists in the project) and feeds the deterministic verifier that checks the generated documentation. extract ( files , graph ) Parameters: files ( list [ str ] ) – analysed source files (paths relative to the root). graph ( dict [ str , list [ str ]] ) – resolved internal dependency graph. Returns: RepoFacts ( RepoFacts ) – the facts sheet plus the vocabulary used for verification. pagerank ( graph , damping = 0.85 , iterations = 50 , tolerance = 1e-09 ) Plain power-iteration PageRank (no external dependency). An edge A -> B means "A imports B", so rank flows towards the modules that many other modules depend on: the structural core of the project. Parameters: graph ( dict [ str , list [ str ]] ) – adjacency list (file -> files it imports). damping ( float , default: 0.85 ) – classic PageRank damping factor. iterations ( int , default: 50 ) – maximum number of iterations. tolerance ( float , default: 1e-09 ) – early-stop threshold on the L1 change between iterations. Returns: dict [ str , float ] – dict[str, float]: rank per node, summing to ~1.0. Grounding FileCard dataclass A compact, one-line description of a file used as prompt evidence. EvidencePacker Packs per-file cards into a text that is guaranteed to fit a token budget. Strategy (a budget-aware, bottom-up "collapse", like a map-reduce summarization that follows the directory structure instead of arbitrary chunks): Group cards by directory. If everything fits the budget, nothing else happens and zero LLM calls are made. Otherwise collapse directories into short summaries, LEAST important first (importance = PageRank of the files they contain), and stop as soon as the text fits. The most central modules therefore keep their full detail. If every directory is already collapsed and it is still too big, lift the blocks one directory level up and repeat (recursive collapse). A final deterministic trim guarantees the budget is respected. The collapse is done with the injected summarizer (an LLM call per block, each call bounded by chunk_budget ). Without a summarizer, or if it fails, a deterministic summary (key files + file names) is used, so packing never crashes the pipeline. pack ( cards , budget ) Parameters: cards ( list [ FileCard ] ) – one card per analysed file. budget ( int ) – maximum estimated tokens of the returned text. Returns: str ( str ) – grouped module notes, important areas placed at the start and at the end. GroundingReport dataclass Outcome of verifying a generated text against the repository vocabulary. feedback () A correction note to append to the query when regenerating the text. GroundingVerifier Checks that every code reference (text in backticks ) in a generated document really exists in the repository. It is a pure-Python existence check, like the "existence ratio" used to evaluate documentation generators: it catches invented file names, classes, functions, libraries, flags and environment variables. It does NOT judge whether a description of behaviour is correct. Complexity: O(L) in the length of the text, each lookup is O(1) on hash sets. __init__ ( facts , evidence_text = '' ) Parameters: facts ( RepoFacts ) – full vocabulary extracted from the repository. evidence_text ( str , default: '' ) – the evidence shown to the LLM; any word appearing in it is also accepted (e.g. names coming from the module notes). verify ( text ) Parameters: text ( str ) – generated markdown. Returns: GroundingReport ( GroundingReport ) – how many references were checked and which are unknown. Utilities TokenUtilities estimate_tokens ( text ) classmethod Cheap, dependency-free, model-agnostic token estimate. Parameters: text ( str ) – text to measure. Returns: int ( int ) – estimated number of tokens (0 for an empty string). arrange_edges_first ( items , key ) Reorder items so the most important ones sit at the START and at the END of the list while the least important end up in the middle. (prevent "lost in the middle" effect) Parameters: items ( list ) – items to reorder. key ( ImportanceScorer ) – Function returning the importance of an item (higher = more important). Returns: list ( list [ T ] ) – the reordered list (a new list, the input is not modified). BaseLanguageTracer Bases: ABC Base interface for the extraction of the dependencies extension abstractmethod property Return the file extension handled by the specific tracer is_useless ( filename ) abstractmethod Define if a file must be ignored extract_dependencies ( file_path , root_dir ) abstractmethod Extract modules names imported inside the file build_module_index ( valid_files ) abstractmethod Create an O(1) index which maps logic modules names to phisical files. Es: 'util.console' -> 'src/utils/console.py' resolve_module_to_file ( module_name , module_index ) abstractmethod Use the index to retrieve the actual module path PythonTracer Bases: BaseLanguageTracer Specific implementation for python, based on AST

The most central modules therefore keep their full detail. If every directory is already collapsed and it is still too big, lift the blocks one directory level up and repeat (recursive collapse). A final deterministic trim guarantees the budget is respected. The collapse is done with the injected summarizer (an LLM call per block, each call bounded by chunk_budget ). Without a summarizer, or if it fails, a deterministic summary (key files + file names) is used, so packing never crashes the pipeline.

docs.text: System Overview RepoWhisper is organized as a facade, source management layer, agent layer, and orchestration layer. Execution phases SourceManager clones a GitHub HTTP(S) repository URL into a temporary local directory. DependencyTracer builds a dependency graph and processing order. CodeNavigator explains each file and returns line-level notes plus a one-line summary. It also receives the one-line summaries of the already analysed modules that the file imports. The local LayaReviewer classifies the draft as EXPLANATION or DEBUG ; a DEBUG draft is sent back to the Navigator. FactsExtractor (no LLM) computes verifiable facts from the code: symbols, third-party imports, entry points, import graph, PageRank, pyproject.toml metadata, README excerpt and CI workflows. EvidencePacker packs the per-file notes into the configured token budget. Architect writes the architectural overview from that grounded evidence (not from the bare directory tree). Storyteller combines the facts, the module notes and the architect draft. GroundingVerifier (no LLM) checks every code reference in the Architect and Storyteller output against the repository. If invented names are found, the agent is asked to regenerate once. The final state is serialized to the documented JSON format. Grounding and token budget The evidence handed to the Architect and the Storyteller is limited by context_budget (estimated tokens, default 6000 ), so every call has a bounded size regardless of the repository size. If the per-file notes fit the budget, no extra LLM call is made. Otherwise the notes are collapsed directory by directory, least central first, using the small PackageSummarizer agent (one bounded call per directory). If it fails, a deterministic summary is used. Important modules are placed at the start and at the end of the prompt. The state contract is defined in orchestration/state.py .
docs.title: System Overview

docs.text: Configuration LLM configuration The facade accepts any LangChain BaseChatModel , so provider configuration is kept outside RepoWhisper: import os from dotenv import load_dotenv from langchain_groq import ChatGroq load_dotenv() llm = ChatGroq( api_key=os.environ["GROQ_API_KEY"], model="openai/gpt-oss-120b", max_tokens=6000, ) The example application loads environment variables with python-dotenv . Use the provider's LangChain integration and pass the resulting model to RepoWhisper . Optional integrations Provider integrations are optional dependencies. Install only the one needed by the application: RepoWhisper[groq] RepoWhisper[ollama] RepoWhisper[openai] RepoWhisper[anthropic] The generated frontend data is written to repowhisper/ui_dist/data.json when analyze() is used. Context budget engine = RepoWhisper(source_target, llm, UserLevel.MID, context_budget=4000) context_budget (default 6000 ) is the maximum estimated number of tokens of evidence given to the Architect and the Storyteller. Lower it for models with a small context window or strict per-minute token limits: the per-file notes are compressed to fit. The model still needs room for its own instructions and output on top of the budget. Token counts are estimated (about 3.5 characters per token), so they are intentionally conservative rather than tokenizer-exact. Laya Reviewer The Reviewer is local and is not configured through LangChain. On first use, RepoWhisper downloads and caches the Vega reader, its backbone model, and the RepoWhisper calibration files. The review step requires no provider API key and does not consume tokens. Source paths engine = RepoWhisper( source_target="https://github.com/...", llm=llm, user_level=UserLevel.JUNIOR, ) source_target is an http://github.com/ or https://github.com/ repository URL. The source manager does not accept local filesystem paths. Repositories are cloned into a temporary directory and removed during cleanup after analysis.

docs.text: Development Run tests .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest The tests are under tests/unit/ and cover agents, the facade, source management, utilities, and workflow behavior. Build documentation .\.venv\Scripts\mkdocs.exe build --strict Preview changes while editing: .\.venv\Scripts\mkdocs.exe serve The generated site/ directory is ignored by Git. Add a supported language RepoWhisper is currently Python-only. Adding another source language requires coordinated changes rather than a tracer-only extension: implement a language-specific tracer derived from BaseLanguageTracer ; register the tracer in DependencyTracer ; add language-specific static facts extraction and grounding vocabulary; teach the tree and source-selection rules about the new file types; add focused tests for parsing, ordering, facts, and grounding; document the language and its limitations. Add an agent New agents should implement the BaseAgent.analyze() contract, receive the LLM through dependency injection, and be wired into AgentsWorkflow with an explicit state contract. Avoid putting provider-specific configuration inside agents. The facade should continue accepting any compatible LangChain chat model.

docs.text: Source Analysis The analysis workflow reads source files directly during the Navigator phase. The dependency tracer determines the processing order and the Navigator sends each selected file to the configured language model for explanation. Dependency graph DependencyTracer walks the repository, parses Python imports with the AST, resolves imports to repository files, and produces a dependency graph. A depth-first traversal generates the file processing order. Circular dependencies are detected and reported instead of recursing indefinitely. Test directories and common virtual-environment, build, and source-control directories are excluded. __init__.py modules are removed from the final processing queue.

docs.text: Installation Requirements Python 3.12. Git, when analyzing a remote repository. An LLM provider supported by LangChain. Network access and cache space for the first-run Laya/Vega reviewer download. Install from PyPI For the standard installation, install the published package from PyPI: python -m pip install repowhisper The base package includes RepoWhisper and its core dependencies. To install RepoWhisper together with the integration for a specific LLM provider, use the corresponding optional dependency: python -m pip install "repowhisper[groq]" python -m pip install "repowhisper[ollama]" python -m pip install "repowhisper[openai]" python -m pip install "repowhisper[anthropic]" Each provider extra includes the base RepoWhisper installation and the provider-specific LangChain integration. Install from the repository For development, or to work with the source code, clone the repository and install the project from its root: uv sync Alternatively, install the local package with pip: python -m pip install . Optional LLM integrations can also be installed from the local checkout: python -m pip install ".[groq]" python -m pip install ".[ollama]" python -m pip install ".[openai]" python -m pip install ".[anthropic]" Install documentation dependencies The development dependency group includes MkDocs and mkdocstrings: uv sync --group dev Build the documentation with: .\.venv\Scripts\mkdocs.exe build --strict Preview it locally with: .\.venv\Scripts\mkdocs.exe serve Credentials Do not commit credentials. Store provider keys in environment variables or a local .env file, which is ignored by Git.

docs.text: Limitations and Troubleshooting Current limitations RepoWhisper currently supports Python code analysis only . It is not a general-purpose analyzer for JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Go, Rust, or other languages. The dependency tracer currently analyzes Python imports and final file processing excludes __init__.py , test directories, virtual environments, build output, and source-control directories. The quality of generated explanations depends on the selected LLM. The grounding verifier detects invented names (files, classes, functions, libraries, flags), not incorrect descriptions of behaviour. Static facts (symbols, imports, entry points) are extracted from Python only. The local Laya Reviewer requires an initial model download and Hugging Face cache space. Large repositories can require substantial time, memory, and model tokens. The bundled HTTP server is intended for local use, not production hosting. analyze() writes generated source data into the bundled UI directory. Common issues No parsable code found Confirm that the target contains .py files and that the path or Git URL is correct. Git clone failure Check that Git is installed and that credentials are available for private repositories. Missing provider package Install the matching optional extra, for example: uv sync --extra groq Missing provider key Set the provider key in the environment before creating the chat model. Never hard-code or commit the key. Documentation import errors Run MkDocs from the repository root and use the project environment: .\.venv\Scripts\mkdocs.exe build --strict

docs.text: Output Format generate_documentation() returns a JSON string. Parse it before consuming the result: import json data = json.loads(engine.generate_documentation() or "{}") The top-level structure is: { "title": "RepoWhisper Analysis", "tree_structure": "...", "narrative": "...", "raw_modules": [] } Top-level fields title Constant title for the generated analysis. tree_structure Textual tree of the analyzed repository, excluding ignored directories. narrative The final architectural narrative generated by the Storyteller agent. raw_modules List of per-file analysis objects: { "file": "src/example.py", "explanation": "The module ...", "code_snippet": "class Example: ...", "notes": { "11": "Creates the service dependency." } } file is the repository-relative path. explanation is the Navigator output, code_snippet contains the analyzed source, and notes maps zero-based line indexes to line-level insights for the UI. Failure behavior The facade returns None when the user interrupts the run. It raises an error when no parsable source is found or when a required processing step fails. Applications should distinguish an empty JSON result from an interrupted or failed analysis.

docs.text: Quick Start RepoWhisper is currently designed for Python code analysis . Source retrieval and static analysis are Python-oriented, and other languages are not yet supported as analysis targets. The facade accepts a source target, an initialized LangChain chat model, and an optional explanation level. from langchain_groq import ChatGroq from repowhisper import RepoWhisper, UserLevel, RepoWhisperError llm = ChatGroq( api_key="read this from an environment variable", model="openai/gpt-oss-120b", max_tokens=6000, ) engine = RepoWhisper( source_target="repo_url", llm=llm, user_level=UserLevel.JUNIOR, ) try: json_data = engine.generate_documentation() except RepoWhisperError as e: print(f"RepoWhisper failed: {e}") generate_documentation() returns a JSON string when analysis succeeds and None when the run is interrupted or cannot produce a result. The configured LLM generates the Architect, Navigator, and Storyteller output. The module review step uses the local Laya/Vega classifier and does not consume LLM tokens. To generate the documentation and open the bundled interface in a browser: engine.analyze() For an application entry point, wrap the call in try/except to handle provider, repository, and server errors without an unhandled traceback: try: engine.analyze() except RepoWhisperError as e: print(f"RepoWhisper failed: {e}") RepoWhisper handles user interruptions internally. Other errors are raised to the caller so that applications can log them or present an appropriate message. The default server port is 8543 . Pass a different port when needed: engine.analyze(port=9000) Place this code in your application entry point. If the entry point is a module inside the repowhisper package, run it from the repository root in module mode (for example, python -m repowhisper.<module> ), rather than running its file directly from inside the package directory. Explanation levels UserLevel changes the amount and style of explanation produced by the Navigator and Storyteller agents: UserLevel.JUNIOR provides detailed, educational explanations. UserLevel.MID focuses on integration, contracts, and state transitions. UserLevel.SENIOR emphasizes trade-offs, performance, and extension points.
docs.title: Quick Start

docs.text: Web Interface RepoWhisper.analyze() serves the bundled frontend locally. engine.analyze() The method: runs the analysis when JSON data path is not supplied; serves the report at /data.json without modifying the bundled UI files; starts an HTTP server bound to the local machine; opens the default browser. The default address is: http://127.0.0.1:8543 Use a custom port with: engine.analyze(port=9000) You can also load an existing data.json file by passing its path. analyze() validates and serializes the report before serving it to the UI: engine.analyze(json_path="data.json") The server runs until interrupted with Ctrl+C and only accepts connections from the local machine. In an application entry point, handle failures around analyze() : try: engine.analyze() except RepoWhisperError as e: print(f"RepoWhisperError failed: {e}") User interruptions are handled by RepoWhisper. Other errors, such as provider, repository, or server failures, are propagated to the caller. Frontend data contract The frontend expects the schema described in Output Format . raw_modules provides source code and explanations, while notes supplies line-level annotations for the code viewer. Operational notes The report served at /data.json contains source code from the analyzed repository. The server is bound to loopback and is not exposed to other devices on the network. Stop the server with Ctrl+C .
